settings.artwork_alt: A typed poem titled The Seasons, with four short verses, one each for summer, autumn, winter and spring.
settings.writeup: I wrote a haiku for every season.
settings.question_1: Which of these seasons would you most like to step into?
settings.question_2: Why do you think Ella chose four tiny poems instead of one long one?
settings.question_3: Which season feels most like home to you?
settings.creative_task: Grab some paper and write a tiny poem about the weather outside right now.

settings.artwork_alt: A watercolour of a smiling pink snail with a green spiral shell, beside yellow and purple flowers in the grass.
settings.writeup: Once upon a time there was a snail and he had friends. When his friends asked to go play with him, he just stared at flowers. He didn't want to play he just wanted to look at flowers. The End.
settings.question_1: What do you think this snail is up to, in among all those flowers?
settings.question_2: If you shrank down to snail size and sat beside it, what would you notice first?
settings.question_3: How do you think the snail is feeling in this spot? What in the drawing makes you say that?
settings.creative_task: Grab some paper and draw a snail's-eye view of somewhere you love. Everything looks bigger from down there.

settings.artwork_alt: A handwritten four line poem about birds darting and twittering, with the word Birds repeated down the left in coloured letters.
settings.writeup: This is my poem. It is about birds.
settings.question_1: If you could ask one of these birds a question, what would it be?
settings.question_2: What might have made Isabelle want to write about birds?
settings.question_3: Where is somewhere you feel as free as a bird?
settings.creative_task: Grab some paper and write a few lines about something you have watched fly.

settings.artwork_alt: A crayon drawing of a smiling girl with long hair, a rainbow arching behind her and a yellow sun, titled My little sister.
settings.question_1: What do you think Aria wanted us to know about her little sister?
settings.question_2: What might her sister say when she sees this drawing?
settings.question_3: Who is someone you look out for, or who looks out for you?
settings.creative_task: Grab some paper and draw someone you know really well, from memory.

settings.artwork_alt: A photo of a round glass fishbowl holding two goldfish, one orange and one white and orange, beside a green plant.
settings.writeup: These are my fish Sunny and Marlo
settings.question_1: What might Sunny and Marlo be up to right now?
settings.question_2: How do you reckon Harvie picked those two names?
settings.question_3: What do you think makes a pet feel safe and happy?
settings.creative_task: Grab some paper and draw the world from inside a fish tank.

settings.artwork_alt: A hand drawn wizard character in a pointed purple hat and round glasses, holding a tall staff, with a speech bubble of three dots.
settings.writeup: I made this character because I love making up new characters. Each day I will do a sketch of an old character and a new character to compare.
settings.question_1: What kind of world do you think this character lives in?
settings.question_2: Where might Sonny find a fresh idea every single day?
settings.question_3: If this character had a worry, who might they go to for help?
settings.creative_task: Grab some paper and invent a character nobody has ever seen before.

settings.artwork_alt: A pencil sketch of a round, happy crocodile character grinning and hugging its belly.
settings.writeup: My mum got me some new pencils and blender set, I drew this straight away.
settings.question_1: What do you think Evelyn wanted to try first with her new pencils?
settings.question_2: Which part of this drawing would you have started with?
settings.question_3: How does it feel to open something brand new and get straight into it?
settings.creative_task: Grab some paper and draw the very first thing that pops into your head.

settings.artwork_alt: A hand drawn dog character standing on two legs in a pink hoodie and yellow trousers, surrounded by colourful letters and numbers.
settings.writeup: What do you call a magic dog? A Labracadabrador.
settings.question_1: What kind of magic would a Labracadabrador get up to around the house?
settings.question_2: What makes a joke really land, do you think?
settings.question_3: Who is someone who can always make you laugh?
settings.creative_task: Grab some paper and invent your own magical animal with a mixed-up name.

settings.artwork_alt: A bright painting of a blue winged creature sitting among yellow flowers on a green background, in a busy, chaotic style.
settings.writeup: This is a drawing that I created in art class. It is of a creature I created, I gave it a style that makes it look, chaotic and looks like it was drawn by a mischevious child.
settings.question_1: Where do you think a creature like this would feel most at home?
settings.question_2: What might have been going through Lucy's head as she made this?
settings.question_3: What might a chaotic, wild creature need from a good friend?
settings.creative_task: Grab some paper and make something messy on purpose, then give it a name.

settings.artwork_alt: A craft bear made from an egg carton with googly eyes, pink pompom cheeks, button ears and pipe cleaner arms, on a blue striped background.
settings.writeup: This is my egg carton bear. I love how the bear looks royal even with a lopsided eye. I think it gives it character.
settings.question_1: What do you think gives this bear its royal look?
settings.question_2: If this bear ruled a kingdom, what would it be like?
settings.question_3: Why do you think Sophie loves the wonky eye so much?
settings.creative_task: Grab some paper and sketch a creature you could build from things in the recycling.

settings.artwork_alt: A coloured pencil portrait of a smiling older man wearing glasses and a blue collared shirt, drawn on lined paper.
settings.writeup: I drew my Pa. He reckons he looks better in real life!
settings.question_1: What do you reckon Pa really thought the first time he saw this?
settings.question_2: What might Remy and his Pa like doing together?
settings.question_3: Who is a grown-up you would love to draw, and why?
settings.creative_task: Grab some paper and draw someone in your family, then show them and see what they say.

settings.artwork_alt: A paper craft house that opens up: the closed side shows a brick house with a blue door, and the open side shows a cosy room where two people sit at a table with flowers, near an apple tree and sunshine.
settings.question_1: Who do you think lives in this house?
settings.question_2: What might be happening in each room right now?
settings.question_3: What makes a house feel safe and cosy to you?
settings.creative_task: Grab some paper and design a house that opens up to show what is inside.

settings.artwork_alt: Two Great Ocean Road holiday photos: one looking up a tall tree trunk into the forest canopy, and one of two people walking a path through a green valley toward the sun between the hills.
settings.writeup: These are a couple of photos that I took when my family went on holiday on the Great Ocean Road recently.
settings.question_1: What do you think made Anouk stop and take each of these?
settings.question_2: If you were standing right there, what might you hear?
settings.question_3: What is a place you have been that you never want to forget?
settings.creative_task: Grab some paper and sketch a view you would want to keep forever.

settings.body: A new prompt every weekday. No account, no login, no printing. Free. Open it and go.
Keep it open in a tab and refresh each morning. It fills the screen the moment it loads, so it is up on your TV before the kids are through the door. No scrolling, no hunting.
One question. Just the creative task. The lot. Use as much or as little as you like and ignore the rest. The prompt is the stimulus, the lesson is yours.

Every prompt starts with a creation from a real Australian kid, moderated by us. Your class looks at art or a story from someone their own age, three open questions and one creative task, pitched for roughly Foundation to Year 6 and easy to take up or down.
After recess, after lunch, or first thing. One creation on the screen and one question turns a hot, restless room into a thinking one, in a couple of minutes.

A daily, low-stakes place to practise real talk. More than one right answer, so every kid can have a go, and the voice you hear is authentically theirs. Do it every day and it becomes part of your class culture, how your room thinks and listens.
Pick a day. Thursday is the day we make something. Kids walk in knowing it, and the ideas start on the way in.
Three questions. The class picks which one they talk about first. A small choice, but it is real student agency, and they own the conversation that follows.
Five minutes or so to talk it out, no rush, then share their thinking. 'I notice, I wonder' gets the quiet kid started.

settings.lead: Run it as a whole lesson
settings.body: When you want it to, it stretches. The questions go in, the creative task comes out the other side. The kid's creation is your mentor text, sitting on the screen the whole time.

settings.question: What is the daily prompt?
settings.answer: A free discussion prompt for the classroom whiteboard, built on a creation a real Australian kid sent in to theINmag. Three open questions and one creative task. A new one every weekday.

settings.question: How do I use it in my classroom?
settings.answer: Put it on the board and let the room go. Whole class, table groups or a settling activity after lunch, whatever fits your day. The prompt is the stimulus, the lesson is yours.

settings.question: Is it free?
settings.answer: Yes. The daily prompt is totally free and separate from theINmag Membership.

settings.question: What year levels is it for?
settings.answer: Roughly Foundation to Year 6, ages 5 to 13. The questions are open, so a Foundation class talks about what they notice and a Year 6 class debates what it means. Adapt up or down as you would anything else.

settings.question: How often does it change?
settings.answer: Every weekday, five a week. Past prompts stay on the page if you missed one or want a run of them. Just tap 'something different' to land on a past one.

settings.question: Where do the creations come from?
settings.answer: Kids across Australia send their art, stories and ideas in to theINmag. Every one is moderated and curated before it goes anywhere near a classroom, so it is all-ages appropriate.

settings.question: Can I use it for speaking and listening?
settings.answer: That is what it is best at. A daily, low-stakes moment of oral language with a real audience, easy to observe and easy to evidence.

settings.question: Do I need a membership?
settings.answer: No. Membership is the printed magazine, posted or emailed three times a year. The daily prompt is free, separate, and does not need one. Having said that, you should probably consider a membership for your room. It's ace!

settings.lede: Put a stock image on the board and you get a shrug. Put up an authentic story or drawing by a real kid and the room leans in, and the talk starts before you have asked a question. It is a mentor text they can enjoy, and the lesson is still yours.
settings.group1_intro: We teach too. So we've made it easy.
settings.group2_intro: There is no right way to run it. One question, the whole thing, or something in between. Take what fits your room today and leave the rest.
